policies.summary: Wind plants over 0.5 MW, other generation over 50 MW and utility-scale storage of 5 MW or more need a PSC certificate of site compatibility, and the certificate cannot override local zoning, so both the state and local zoning must approve.

Sites for PSC-certified wind facilities must exclude land within 1.1 times turbine height of a nonparticipating owner's property line and within 3 times turbine height of a nonparticipating owner's inhabited rural residence, unless all parties agree to a variance; local zoning may require more.

restrictions.description: Need for county staff to draft permitting ordinances for data centers, solar energy, and battery facilities. Active. Legal basis: County Commission motion (no numbered resolution issued). Per the signed official March 18, 2026 minutes: "Planning and Zoning Board would like to put a 12-month moratorium on data centers, solar energy and battery facilities. This would help the board to get the ordinances updated. Motion by Commissioner Pelton, seconded by Commissioner Kleemann to accept the moratorium as presented up to one year." All members present (Heiser, Olson, Pelton, Dolezal, Kleemann) voted aye. Preceded by a March 10, 2026 Planning & Zoning Board recommendation to the Commission on the same terms.

Geronimo Power (through affiliated LLCs including CCDC LLC) has purchase agreements for roughly 2,072 acres in Harmony Township and 934 acres in neighboring Durbin Township, and is pursuing a data center and a 200-MW battery energy storage system in the township in addition to an already-under-construction 200-MW solar facility (Harmony Solar); residents raised concerns about tonal noise, property values, water use, road traffic, organic-farming impacts, and inadequate study of impacts, and about a conflict of interest (a former township board chair who did not recuse himself from 2025-2026 zoning-ordinance votes had a pending land-purchase agreement with a Geronimo Power affiliate). Pending as of 2026-09-23. The Township Board voted unanimously on 2026-09-22 to hold a public hearing on whether a two-year moratorium on industrial-scale development (data centers, battery storage, solar, wind, transmission lines, gas generation) is appropriate; no hearing date had been set. The board separately voted to seek a legal review of 2025-2026 zoning-ordinance amendments that eased approval conditions for the proposed data center, including whether a conflict of interest by a then-board-chair voids those amendments, and whether the pending conditional use permit applications for the data center and battery storage facility remain legally eligible for consideration pending that review. Legal basis: Not yet enacted. On 2026-09-22 the Township Board unanimously passed a motion (moved by Board Chair Dustin Burchill) to hold a formal public hearing on whether to adopt a two-year moratorium; the specific ordinance language has not been finalized.

Commissioners raised concerns about the impact of large-scale wind and solar construction traffic on county-maintained roads and bridges (heavy loads, vehicles exceeding weight restrictions) after TransAlta announced and then dropped plans for a wind farm in the county; the county wanted road-use agreements and oversight in place before any wind or solar developer (including Orsted, whose Badger Wind Farm spans McIntosh and Logan counties) could use county roads for construction. Extended as of 2026-06-01 per the McIntosh Democrat; long-form reporting by Canary Media (2026-09) and Mother Jones (2026-09) independently describes McIntosh County as having 'adopted a one-year moratorium on new wind projects' in April 2026 -- a description that may refer to this same road-use moratorium (simplified) or to a distinct action not otherwise located in this pass. As of 2026-09-23 the road-use restriction on wind/solar construction traffic remains the confirmed, sourced instrument. [VERIFY instrument number; primary source (news-only evidence) not confirmed at confidence 0.55 in the 2026-09 refresh]. Legal basis: McIntosh County Board of County Commissioners motion/action, first enacted July 2025 and extended by vote on 2026-06-01 (instrument/resolution number not located).

projects.description: Dickinson Wind applied for a conditional use permit to construct an 87-turbine, 150-MW facility in Stark County.

In June 2019, the PSC rejected NextEra’s application to construct the Burke County Wind Project due to proximity to wetlands and potential wildlife impacts, the first time the PSC had rejected a wind farm application.
PNE Wind proposed a 70-turbine wind farm in Burleigh County near Morton Township.
Orion Renewable Energy Ground submitted a zoning application for a 114-turbine, 383-MW project in Billings County.

A developer purchased Coal Creek Station, North Dakota’s largest coal-fired power plant, in 2022, averting its closure, and put plans into place to develop Coal Creek Wind Farm, a 400-MW wind farm in the area.
In April 2024, the McLean County Board of Commissioners denied a zoning permit for the Discovery Wind Farm, a 94-turbine wind farm proposed by Apex Clean Energy.
In 2018, Capital Power proposed a 152-MW wind farm in Mercer County.
